I am 53 years old, and I have been farming my whole life here in Quzhou County. My family has about 6 mu of flat, good-quality land that we irrigate from the village well. I did not go to high school, but I know this land and this rotation better than any book.

Last October, after the autumn harvest, I rotary-tilled the fields and sowed winter wheat using improved seed I saved from the year before — about 15 kg per mu. The wheat is already in the ground, and now that spring has arrived, it is greening up. I will topdress it with urea at jointing, then irrigate three times total: once now at regreening, once at heading, and once at grain filling. I also need to spray twice for insects and once for weeds; if the weather turns damp, I will add one fungicide spray to prevent rust. I expect about 500 kg per mu at harvest in early June.

As soon as the wheat comes off, I will plant summer maize directly into the stubble without any ploughing — there is no time to waste, and no-tillage works fine if you manage it right. I will buy hybrid seed from the shop in town, about one package per mu. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat because the wheat stubble feeds the soil, but I will still put down compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice — at the big喇叭口 stage and during grain filling — and spray twice for insects and once for weeds. With good weather, I should get about 550 kg per mu by October.

I do not grow cotton or vegetables on my main land. The wheat-maize double crop is what this land is made for, and it gives me two harvests and steady income. I have been doing it for thirty years, and I see no reason to change.
